key_points: The initial request (CL-01, from SH-CX) was to build a chatbot explaining parcel lateness to customers. Investigation redefined the problem (PD-1) as warehouse RELEASE-BATCH job failures, not carrier delay.
SH-LOG's claim (CL-02/E-03) that carrier pickup delay causes lateness was CONTRADICTED by evidence E-01, E-02, E-04, E-06; hypothesis H-CARRIER-PICKUP-DELAY was REJECTED.

Evidence shows 300/1000 orders (30%) late at handover (E-01) and RELEASE-BATCH failed 21/30 runs with 290 orders released after scheduled pickup (E-04); carrier pickup delay is only a 2h median (E-02, E-06), too small to explain the 30% figure. H-WAREHOUSE-DELAY and H-WMS-BATCH-FAILURE are SUPPORTED.

What was released (SD-1 release_scope): diagnose_release_batch_failures:DA-WMS and verify_handoff_integrity:H-PICK. The customer-facing chatbot (explain_lateness_cause_to_customers) and order-level correlation were NOT released.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS and verification found VOB-R-2 (blocking verify_handoff_integrity:H-PICK, required BEFORE_RELEASE) still OPEN: H-PICK delivery_status/semantic_validity remain UNKNOWN even after the mechanical pickup_by_slot query (W-WI-VERIFY-HANDOFF) ran.

VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-CORRELATION (HIGH impact) is also OPEN but its blocking_scope (correlate_order_level_lateness, explain_lateness_cause_to_customers) lies outside the actually released scope, so it did not force a hold on what was released.
No hold was applied (release.hold is empty); instead the release proceeded with the open issues documented as known limitations.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a clean pass; some items were deferred into Verification Obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved.

VOB-R-2 is OPEN and blocks exactly the released verify_handoff_integrity:H-PICK scope item: it is unknown whether the Shop→Carrier handoff is reliable, since pickup_by_slot (E-06) only measures delay magnitude, not delivery or semantic integrity.

VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-CORRELATION is OPEN and blocks correlate_order_level_lateness and explain_lateness_cause_to_customers (the original chatbot request, CL-01); these cannot ship until the 290 late-released orders (E-04) are confirmed at order-id level to overlap with the 300 handover-late orders (E-01).

The actual RELEASE-BATCH fix (remedy SR-R1-FIX-RELEASE-BATCH, assigning SH-WMS to diagnose/patch the job) is unfinished and marked not feasible in contest time; the root cause of the 21/30 failures (U-BATCH-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE) remains unresolved.
Carrier-side pickup delay (median 2h, E-02/E-06) is confirmed too small to explain the 30% handover-stage lateness (E-01); any carrier-focused fix alone would be insufficient.
The interim manual force-release remedy (SR-R2) has unverified reliability, so residual lateness may persist even where applied.

Completeness of all three underlying data assets (DA-ORD, DA-WMS, DA-PICK) is UNKNOWN (U-DATA-COMPLETENESS), which limits confidence in the headline 30%, 290-order, and 2h figures used to justify the release.

The link between the 290 orders released late (E-04) and the 300 orders recorded late at handover (E-01) is only an unverified assumption (A-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP) based on matching magnitude, not a confirmed order-level join.
output.summary: The requester (SH-CX) asked for a chatbot explaining parcel lateness to customers (CL-01). Investigation defined the real problem (PD-1) as warehouse-side: RELEASE-BATCH failed in 21 of 30 runs, causing 290 orders to be released after their scheduled pickup (E-04), which lines up with the 300/1000 orders (30%) recorded late at the Shop→Carrier handover stage (E-01). The logistics lead's claim that a 2-hour carrier pickup delay is the cause (CL-02/E-03) was CONTRADICTED by evidence (E-01, E-02, E-04, E-06) and the corresponding hypothesis (H-CARRIER-PICKUP-DELAY) was REJECTED, since the 2h median delay (E-02, E-06) is too small to explain 30% handover lateness; H-WAREHOUSE-DELAY and H-WMS-BATCH-FAILURE are SUPPORTED instead. What was actually released is a narrower scope than the original request: diagnosis of the RELEASE-BATCH failures (DA-WMS) and an attempt to verify handoff integrity (H-PICK) — not the customer-facing chatbot or order-level correlation, which remain blocked. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS and the verify step flagged that VOB-R-2, which blocks exactly the released verify_handoff_integrity:H-PICK item and is required BEFORE_RELEASE, is still OPEN (H-PICK's delivery_status/semantic_validity remain UNKNOWN despite the mechanical query W-WI-VERIFY-HANDOFF completing). A second open obligation, VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-CORRELATION, blocks the chatbot and correlation work but sits outside the released scope, so release proceeded on the narrower scope with that work still unshipped. No hold was applied (release.hold is empty); the release instead carries a documented list of known limitations covering the open VOBs, unresolved RELEASE-BATCH root cause, unverified data completeness, and the unconfirmed order-level overlap assumption.
